Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tri-region technical deep-dive: finding a 2-hour overlap

Hi all —

Thanks again for carving out time to get the architects and our solutions team together. To make this concrete: we need a 90–120 minute technical deep-dive (architecture walk, performance expectations, and KV/cache handoff discussion) with 2nd‑line architects and one of our SREs.

Because the group spans US / EU / APAC and daylight-savings is in play for parts of the org, I sketched three UTC anchor options that create different local windows. Attached is a compact timezone_matrix.xlsx (anchored to UTC) and a small PNG showing the usable overlap: availability-utc-anchor.png.

Options (all times shown as UTC — local equivalents underneath):

A) 14:00–16:00 UTC
   - US West (PDT): 07:00–09:00
   - US East (EDT): 10:00–12:00
   - EU (BST): 15:00–17:00
   - APAC (SG/HKT): 22:00–00:00 (late)

B) 18:00–20:00 UTC
   - US West (PDT): 11:00–13:00
   - US East (EDT): 14:00–16:00
   - EU (BST): 19:00–21:00
   - APAC (SG/HKT): 02:00–04:00 (next day — early)

C) 06:00–08:00 UTC
   - US West (PDT): 23:00–01:00 (previous day — late)
   - US East (EDT): 02:00–04:00
   - EU (BST): 07:00–09:00
   - APAC (SG/HKT): 14:00–16:00

Quick notes:
- Option A favors EU daytime and US morning, but pushes APAC late (might be okay for one-off deep-dive).
- Option B is centered on US daytime and EU evening; APAC would need a very early slot.
- Option C is APAC-friendly and EU morning, but is rough for US participants.

Ask: please indicate which option you can support (+ any hard no's for people we must include). If none of the three work, tell us the tightest 2-hour window that includes at least one APAC and one US participant and we will try a one-off weekend slot.

I left a short mutual-action-plan draft (mutual-action-plan-draft.pdf) with proposed attendees and agenda — we can update after consensus on timing.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Vivek — thanks for the concise options. Short answer: Option B looks the least bad for our US architects (they prefer 14:00–16:00 local), but Pierre (France) can't do anything starting after 20:30 CET most days, and our APAC lead (Li Mei) has teaching commitments in the early morning.

If we push B later by 30 minutes (18:30–20:30 UTC) that keeps US happy and gives EU a tiny bit more buffer, but makes APAC even rougher. If it's possible to move one attendee (we can float a backup APAC architect), we're open to Option A if APAC can accept 1 late evening.

I've attached a short constraints doc that lists hard blockers for our engineers (customer_constraints.docx). The priority for us is to have Pierre + one APAC person + a Redwood SRE in the room.

Can you ping Li Mei to confirm her absolute earliest availability?

—Alex
